node.title: Re: What does $, = " " do in this code?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [alwynpan],

The special variable [doc://$,] controls what [doc://print] outputs between its arguments. See also [doc://$"] and [doc://$\].

local $" = "a"; # list separator local $, = "c"; # output field separator local $\ = "l"; # output record separator my @x = ('F','O'); print @x, "@x", "x"; # prints "FcOcFaOcxl"

So [doc://$"] controls what is inserted between elements when the array @x is interpolated into a string. Normally, it'd turn out to be "F O", but since we've redefined [doc://$"], we get "FaO".

Next, [doc://$,] controls what gets output between the arguments of [doc://print]. Since the argument list is "flattened" and the elements of the array @x each become an argument to the function, the above is as if we had written print "F", "O", "FaO", "x" (this is a little bit of a simplification but good enough in this example). So the value of [doc://$,] is inserted in between every argument.

Lastly, [doc://$\] is simply what [doc://print] outputs at the end of the argument list. It can be useful to set it to something like "\n", but note that this affects every [doc://print] statement, which is why doing so is not always a good idea in larger programs. That's also why I've used [doc://local] above, because that'll limit the effect of the assignment to the current dynamic scope only.

As you can see variable names can be special characters, but Perl already uses a lot of them for special meanings, so you shouldn't try and make your own! Just use the ones Perl provides, when you need to. See [doc://perlvar]. Update: Also, [shmem] [id://1175028|makes an excellent point!]

By the way, the code you posted shows some fairly advanced techniques, I would not recommend it as something to study for your "first day"!

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
